flags.reason: The Bank loader concatenates the held-out test features and labels into X_train/y_train before fitting both the discriminator and counterfactual models, directly leaking the evaluation set into training.
The GMC loader appends X_test/y_test to X_train/y_train and then still evaluates on that same test set, causing direct train-test leakage.

Counterfactuals are flattened factual-by-factual, but factual rows are paired with them using np.tile rather than np.repeat, so sparsity, actionability, and proximity compare almost every CF to the wrong factual point.

predict_proba applies ReLU to logits and normalizes the positive parts instead of using the softmax assumed by CrossEntropyLoss, making classifier probabilities and the 0.55 confidence filter invalid.

The sole configured mask contains only 1e-3 values, but the evaluation marks immutable features only where mask == 1, producing an empty mask and an actionability score that is vacuously 1 for every CF.

Generated categorical one-hot/quantile coordinates are evaluated directly without projection to valid categories, so validity and proximity can reward off-manifold fractional categorical values even though only the saved CSV is decoded.

The advertised p-norm sweep includes p=0.01 (not a norm), and the code raises the weighted sum to 1/p=100, making the 1e-3-masked distances numerically collapse or explode and corrupt nearest-neighbor selection.

train_multiclass_counterfactual_flow_model ignores its flow_model_class argument and always constructs ContinuousNormalizingFlow, despite the caller explicitly passing MaskedAutoregressiveFlow and the API documenting that choice.
After assigning below-threshold candidates infinite distance, argsort still takes exactly n_nearest entries; when fewer qualify, rejected low-confidence points silently re-enter the training targets.
action_mask is declared optional with default None but its .shape is accessed unconditionally, so CFMetrics crashes for the documented/default invocation (including the repository's own tests).

The metrics named proximity_continuous_* call feature_distance without setting categorical_metric=None, so its default Jaccard term is included and the reported values are not continuous-only proximity.

NaN outputs are replaced by resampling other generated outputs before coverage/quality evaluation, hiding generation failures; if every row has a NaN the loop may never terminate, while an entirely-NaN batch bypasses repair.
Early stopping treats test_loss < min_test_loss + eps as an improvement and overwrites min_test_loss even with a worse loss, repeatedly saving degraded density models and resetting patience.

Sampling returns the flow output unchanged and never copies or clamps immutable coordinates to the factual values, so the claimed actionability constraints are not actually enforced at inference time.

Generation indexes the class one-hot vector by the raw target label, whereas training uses classes.index(label), so the purported generic multiclass API fails or conditions on the wrong class for non-contiguous labels.

GroupedBatchDataLoader groups batch_size already-batched tensors per yield but reports len(self.batches), so batch_size=256 can flatten thousands of examples at once and all reported/early-stopping losses are divided by the wrong number of iterations.

Lending Club (like Bank, GMC, and Default) discards CSV ground truth for stored y_*_pred arrays, then the main script calls agreement of a newly trained surrogate with those predictions discriminator accuracy; Adult alone uses true labels.
No diversity metric or equivalent evaluation exists although the README repeatedly claims superior diversity and each factual receives multiple samples.
No baseline implementations or comparison runner/results are present despite the README's claim that extensive experiments show DiCoFlex outperforms existing methods.
The experiment seeds only NumPy, leaving PyTorch initialization, dropout, and sampling uncontrolled, so the advertised all-dataset experiment is not reproducible from a single run configuration.
